chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad narrated from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hudhayfah ibn Mansur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Food was scarce during the time of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so the Muslims came and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, food has become scarce, and nothing remains of it except with so-and-so, so order him to sell it.' He said, then he praised Allah and extolled Him, and then said: 'O so-and-so, indeed the Muslims have mentioned that food has become scarce except for a little with you, so bring it out and sell it as you wish, and do not withhold it.'

key_terms.عَهْدِ: during the time of / era of

ai.seo_question: What was the Prophet's instruction regarding food scarcity and market withholding?
ai.summary: This hadith from the chapter on *Hukrah* (withholding goods to drive up prices) illustrates the Prophet’s pragmatic approach to market regulation during scarcity, emphasizing the moral obligation to release essential goods rather than hoarding them. It highlights the distinction between legitimate profit-seeking and the unethical practice of withholding necessities, a key concept in Shia commercial jurisprudence. The narrative underscores the Prophet's direct authority in guiding economic behavior to ensure public welfare.
